sentences.text: This criminal revision petition u/s 397 Cr.PC has been filed by the revisionist against the order dated 03.01.2022 passed by the court of Ld. MM, South East District, Saket Courts, New Delhi, in complaint case No. 636652/2016 titled as "Yash Choudhary Vs. Mohit Gogia & Ors" vide which complaint filed by the revisionist was dismissed.

entities.label: COURT

entities.text: Yash Choudhary Vs. Mohit Gogia & Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 2. By filing the present revision petition, revisionist seeks to set aside the impugned dismissal order dated 03.01.2022 passed by the Ld. Trial Court.

3. Brief facts of the case, as stated in the revision petition, are that revisionist was looking for investor for one of his project of Shipra Estate Limited situated at 10/2, Niti Khand, Indirapuram,
Ghaziabad and respondent no.3 approached him that he can arrange the funds of Rs.225 crore required for the development of the said project and for this he required certain amount from the revisionist as commitment amount.

On 10.02.2015 after getting convinced by respondent no.3,
revisionist gave Rs.30 lakhs in cash to him in presence of Sushil Kumar Katiyar and as counter guarantee, the respondent gave him post dated cheques.

He also told the revisionist that revisionist may give him Rs.20 lakhs more so that he and Mr. Gogia can have bonafide trust, so, on 20.05.2015 he paid another amount of Rs.20 lakhs in cash to the respondents.
Respondents did not honour the deal and no investment money was arranged by them.
The revisionist has presented the cheques given by respondent but same got dishonoured with remark "Insufficient Funds".
The revisionist gave a complaint to SHO PS Chitranjan Park but no action was taken.
Thus, revisionist filed a complaint u/s. 200 Cr.PC alongwith an application under Section 156(3) Cr.P.C before Ld. Trial Court for registration of FIR.
4. Application u/s. 156(3) Cr.PC

was dismissed vide order dated 22.06.2017 and complainant led his pre-summoning evidence and u/s. 200 Cr.PC examined only himself as CW-1 and Ld. Trial Court dismissed the complaint u/s. 200 Cr.PC vide impugned order dated 03.01.2022 and did not issue process against the accused persons.

5. Feeling aggrieved from the impugned order, complainant filed present revision petition on the ground that Ld. Trial Court has completely ignored the inducement by the respondents and that the security cheques were given by respondent no.2 and 3 in order to gain trust of revisionist to get his money.

The revisionists had entrusted the respondent No. 2 and 3 with an amount of Yash Chowdhury vs State Of Nct Of Delhi on 6 December, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/126523114/
1 Rs.50,00,000/- for the processing of Rs.250 Crores loan for a project and same was secured by security cheques.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Once the loan was not processed and the amount of Rs 50,00,000/- was not returned, it tantamounts to breach of trust.

Ld Trial Court has failed to appreciate the evidence led by the Revisionists which discloses the commission of an offence u/s. 406 IPC.
6.
Case file and TCR perused.
Detailed arguments heard.
7. The impugned order was passed u/s. 203 Cr.PC, which is reproduced hereinbelow:
"203. Dismissal of complaint.

If, after considering the statements on oath (if any) of the complainant and of the witnesses and the result of the inquiry or investigation (if any) under section 202, the Magistrate is of opinion that there is no sufficient ground for proceeding, he shall dismiss the complaint, and in every such case he shall brieftly record his reasons for so doing."
8. Section 203 consists of two parts.

The first part lays down the materials which is to be considered by Magistrate and the second part says that if after considering those materials, Magistrate in his judgment, do not find any sufficient ground for proceeding, then he shall dismiss the complaint.
9. In the present case, the only material before the Magistrate was the testimony of complainant as CW-1.

As per his testimony through one of his known i.e. Sushil Kumar Katiyar, both respondents approached him and assured him to secure loan of Rs.250 crores for development of a project and asked for processing fund of Rs.50 lacs, which he gave to respondent no.2 & respondent no.3 and in lieu of that they gave him four cheques as security.
When respondents could not get the loan processed then he presented the cheques out of which cheques amounting to Rs.30 lacs got dishonoured.
He did not give any details of the other cheques received from the respondents or how he made payment of Rs.50 lacs to them.
He could have easily examine Sushil Kumar Katiyar as he was known to him and well aware of the facts.
But he failed to mention his name in his list of witnesses.
His allegations are not supported by even an iota of substantive material.

10. The court is also concurs with the observation made by the Ld. Trial Court that "the evidence of the complainant is silent about any dishonest inducement for delivery of the said sums of money exercised by the accused persons on the complainant which is an essential element of the offence of cheating and dishonestly inducing delivery of property punishable u/s 420 IPC.

From the evidence led by the complainant it has also not been shown that the accused persons had been entrusted with the said sum of Rs.50 lacs which is the essential ingredient of the offence of criminal breach of trust punishable u/s 406 IPC.

There has been stated no fact by the complainant to show that the accused persons or either of them had committed forgery of any document for the purpose of cheating or they have used as genuine any forged document.
Therefore the commission of the offence punishable u/s 468/471 IPC is also not made out."

sentences.text: It is to be kept in mind that revision jurisdiction is normally to be exercised in exceptional cases where there is a glaring defect in procedure or there is manifest error of law and consequently there has been a flagrant miscarriage of justice.
The order passed by Ld. MM is a speaking order.

If impugned order is analyzed in light of scope of section 397/399 Cr.P.C, no wrong, illegality,
impropriety or irregularity is noticed therein.
12. Accordingly, in view of the above observations, the present revision petition is dismissed.
There is no illegality and infirmity in the order dated 03.01.2022 passed by Ld. Trial Court.
13. TCR alongwith copy of this order be sent back to the concerned Ld. Trial Court / Successor Court.
14. Revision file be consigned to the Record Room after due compliance.
Vipin Digitally signed by  Vipin Kharb
